explanations: failure() logs the error as { ...err }. An Error's name, message and stack are not own enumerable properties, so the spread copies nothing for a plain Error and the log line contains "error": {}. Every flush failure is logged without its cause, which makes outages of the time-series store very hard to diagnose. It should copy the fields explicitly, e.g. { name: err.name, message: err.message, stack: err.stack }.
out() spreads base and data first and then sets service, level and event, so the logger's own values overwrite caller-supplied keys. Nothing validates or rejects reserved keys.

Number.isFinite(NaN) is false, so those 3 are skipped and counted; the other 7 are pushed. After the loop a single readings.dropped warn is emitted with the counts, and the return is readings.length - dropped = 7.

The catch calls this.buffer.unshift(...batch), restoring the readings at the front ahead of anything accepted meanwhile, and finally resets flushing so the next flush can retry. It is not discarded or appended at the end.
